Verified directly against the source — `isEnabled` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts:21` is the sole flag-evaluation predicate. I confirmed the trickier cases by reading the files: `readFlag` (`src/hooks/flag-context.ts`) reads a snapshot and only falls back to `isEnabled` for missing keys, so `useFeatureFlag` and `FeatureGate` (which call `readFlag`, not `isEnabled`) are correctly excluded, despite both carrying a misleading "Must call: isEnabled" comment. `FeatureFlagProvider` and the layout/tenant-context files that build the snapshot also never call `isEnabled` directly, so they're excluded too. Everywhere else — API routes, dashboard pages, server jobs/services, actions, and several components using a `flags.x === true || isEnabled(...)` fallback pattern — does call `isEnabled` by name directly.
